title: Recent Fire Frequency and Woody Species Composition Beyond Vegetation Types: A Landsat–Sentinel-2 Analysis in the Péni Classified Forest (Burkina Faso)
content: In Sudanian savannas, associations between fire frequency and woody species composition may reflect differences between vegetation types. We analyzed woody cover data from 213 plots surveyed in 2021 in the Péni Classified Forest, Burkina Faso. A Landsat model calibrated on Sentinel-2 was used to reconstruct the number of burned seasons from 2013–2014 to 2019–2020. Compared with fire scars recorded in the field, Landsat detections had a recall of 75% and a specificity of 81%. MODIS detected 2.8% of the plot-seasons classified as burned by Sentinel-2. Fire frequency was associated with 7.56% of the floristic variation, 1.00% after controlling for survey month and space, and 0.18% after vegetation types were added. Depending on the fire measure, this contribution ranged from 0.11 to 0.28%. In the savannas, no association with any species or structural attribute remained after correction for multiple testing. Recent fire frequency therefore adds little floristic information, although a historical role of fire cannot be ruled out. This fire history can guide monitoring, but repeated surveys that include regeneration are needed to assess vegetation change and resilience.
